_comment: One home for the facts every surface restates: which bridges exist, on which port,
under which name, stateful or not, and what each one reaches. scripts/facts_check.py
verifies the surfaces listed below against this file. Change the manifest first,
then the surfaces; the check fails until they agree.

Filesystem roots are launcher-derived on both platforms: the tooling root comes from the launcher's own location (COWORK_ROOT), Downloads from the user profile, and the config root from COWORK_CONFIG_ROOT set in the gitignored Startup/cowork-env.cmd or Startup/posix/cowork-env.sh. The roots below are the Windows variable names as they appear in fs-server.cmd; the POSIX launcher passes $COWORK_ROOT, $HOME/Downloads and $COWORK_CONFIG_ROOT.

Files that still carry the repository placeholder YOURUSER (the watchdog, the connector manifests, the shipped jobs, the skills) are personalized by scripts/copilot/personalize.py; no launcher, task file or root in this manifest does.
connector_id is the tool namespace the skills address; plugin_manifest is the Cowork connector package that must carry it and the port.

stdio is the Windows launcher; stdio_posix is its macOS/Linux sibling under Startup/posix, present only for a bridge whose platforms include macos - now the Command bridge alone. facts_check.py verifies each exists and that neither hard-codes a root.

products and platforms are two different cuts and every bridge carries both. As of 2026-09-15 only the Command bridge runs under Claude Cowork: the Playwright and Filesystem bridges are Copilot Cowork on Windows only, because Claude Cowork ships browsing and connected-folder file access first-party and the repository bridges only duplicated them. 8934 Power Automate was already Copilot/Windows. Bridge counts are DERIVED from these lists and never stated - four for the whole repository, one for any Claude Cowork surface, one for any macOS surface.

scopes lists the surfaces written for one product or platform. facts_check.py checks each against the bridges that exist for it: the port and the '<name> bridge' of every bridge outside the scope are stale phrases there, on top of the scope's own count words.

The watchdog and personalizer are Copilot Cowork on Windows only. Claude Cowork owns stdio server lifetime and has no tunnel ports to watch; the hosted-route personalizer lives at scripts/copilot/personalize.py.

Third-party inference behind Claude Cowork changes the model, not the host: the bridge scope above is unchanged. If an administrator removes the host's built-in file or browser tools, the Windows launchers still exist and the POSIX launchers can be restored from 6cfc77c; register only what the host then lacks. Skills are not scoped by product; see docs/skills-by-configuration.md.
